chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', from Aban, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from a man, from Razin, who said:

I was performing ablution in the washing basin of Kufa when a man came, placed his shoes, and placed his whip upon them. Then he approached and performed ablution with me. I bumped him, and he fell onto his hands. He arose and performed ablution. When he finished, he struck my head with the whip three times, then said: 'Beware of bumping, lest you break (a bone) and incur compensation.' I said, 'Who is this?' They said, 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him).' I went to offer my excuses to him, but he passed by and did not turn towards me.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.تَغْرِيم: Incurring financial compensation or blood money
key_terms.دِرَّة: A type of whip or cane used by leaders
key_terms.مِيضَاة: Washing basin or fountain for ablution

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Imam Ali (AS) striking a man's head with his whip in Kufa?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the practical application of 'adab' (etiquette) in public worship spaces, where Imam Ali (peace be upon him) corrected a minor physical encroachment during ablution to prevent potential injury and financial liability (gharamah). The Imam's subsequent silence upon the narrator's apology highlights the distinction between correcting a specific action and maintaining dignified composure, a nuance valued in Shia jurisprudence regarding social interactions. It serves as a key example of the Imam's attentiveness to both physical comfort and legal implications in communal religious settings.
